value: After être, un and une are kept in the negative (Ce n'est pas un problème)
Only the article changes to de; the noun itself is not replaced

evidence.notes: First entry is the standard exception to de-negation; the second clarifies the transformation given in the rule.

value: ne and pas surround the auxiliary, never the past participle
Pronominal verbs place the reflexive pronoun between ne and the auxiliary

evidence.notes: First entry is the stated word order and trap; the pronominal placement is standard usage.

value: ne and pas form a unit before the infinitive and are never split
With a conjugated verb, ne and pas normally surround the verb instead

evidence.notes: First entry is the stated formation and trap; the second is the contrast with conjugated verbs.

value: Definite articles (le, la, l', les) are kept after ni
Indefinite and partitive articles disappear after ni
With a single negated noun, pas de replaces ni

evidence.notes: First two entries are the stated article behaviour; the single-noun limit is standard usage.

proposals.entity_key: Negative duration: passé composé instead of present
value: In affirmative sentences with depuis, the present tense is used
The imparfait is used when the duration runs up to a past point

evidence.notes: First entry is the general rule this is an exception to; the imparfait counterpart is standard usage.

value: ne precedes the reflexive pronoun, not the verb alone
In compound tenses ne and pas surround the auxiliary, with the pronoun before it

evidence.notes: First entry is the stated word order and trap; the compound-tense placement is standard usage.

value: In the affirmative imperative the pronoun follows the verb
ne precedes the pronoun and pas follows the verb

evidence.notes: Both entries follow from the rule's word order and its contrast with the affirmative.

value: In the affirmative imperative the pronoun follows the verb with a hyphen
The object pronoun comes between ne and the verb

evidence.notes: Both entries follow from the stated word order, condition, and trap.

proposals.entity_key: No futur simple after 'si' in future condition
value: The futur antérieur is also excluded after si when si means 'if'
si meaning 'whether' may be followed by the future

evidence.notes: First entry is stated in the rule; the second is the stated restriction on when si means 'whether'.

value: me, te, nous, vous precede le, la, les
le, la, les precede lui, leur
en comes in second position, after the other object pronoun

evidence.notes: First two entries come from the rule's formation and trap; the position of en is standard usage.
